summary: Describes how a SIP response can carry a Q.850 cause code in a Reason header field. Some deployments already did this for failures on calls gatewayed to the phone network, and this document writes down the practice formally. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: When a phone call fails, the old phone network gives a reason number. This tells internet phone calls how to pass that same number along, so people know why the call failed.

subtitle: Carry telephone network failure codes in SIP responses.

tldr.problem: When SIP calls are gatewayed to traditional telephone networks (PSTN), the telephone system provides Q.850 cause codes explaining why calls failed, but SIP had no standardized way to convey these codes back to the caller.
tldr.mechanism: Formally specify use of the SIP Reason header field (defined in RFC 3326) to carry Q.850 cause codes in SIP responses, documenting existing deployment practice.
tldr.outcome: VoIP systems can now transparently pass telephone network failure information to callers, helping them understand why calls failed.

today: RFC 6432 is a Standards Track document. The use of Reason header fields with Q.850 codes is now the formal standard for SIP-to-PSTN gateway interoperability and is widely implemented.

sections.title: The gateway problem
sections.content: Many VoIP systems gateway SIP calls to traditional PSTN telephone networks. When a PSTN call fails, the telephone system provides a Q.850 cause code indicating the reason: busy, unreachable, forbidden, etc. However, RFC 3326 defined the SIP Reason header field in general terms without specifying its use for Q.850 codes. Nonetheless, deployed systems were already using the Reason header to carry Q.850 codes, and this RFC documents that practice formally.
sections.eli5: Phone companies have a system of numbers that explain why a call failed. Internet phone systems needed a way to pass those numbers along to the internet side.

sections.title: Using Reason with Q.850
sections.content: Any SIP response message except 100 (Trying) may contain a Reason header field with a Q.850 cause code. The 100 (Trying) response is excluded because it is transmitted hop by hop rather than end to end. The Reason header field format is specified in RFC 3326, and RFC 6432 adds the normative use of this header for Q.850. Applications processing the Reason header should be aware that an incorrect Q.850 code could cause problems—for instance, an announcement system might play the wrong message based on the code.
sections.eli5: Any response message can have a Reason header with a Q.850 code, except the quick 'trying' response. The code tells the caller why the call didn't work.

sections.title: Protecting the Reason header
sections.content: The Reason header field should be protected by a suitable integrity mechanism to prevent tampering. Transport-layer security (TLS) or network-layer security (IPsec) with appropriate cipher suites can satisfy this requirement. Without such protection, an attacker could modify the Q.850 code, potentially causing the wrong announcement to play or misleading the caller about the actual failure reason.
sections.eli5: Since the code affects what message people hear, it should be encrypted so nobody can trick the system into lying about why the call failed.
